display.title: Brachos and Hashem's Name: Rabbi Moshe Galante and the Sheikh's Secret
display.summary_short: Why we pay Hashem for our food with a brachah, from Avraham Avinu's tent to a boy's cupcake, and the end of the story of Rabbi Moshe Galante and the sheikh who honored Hashem's Name.
display.summary_long: For Parshas Vayeira, the storyteller describes Avraham Avinu's hospitality in the desert: guests who would not bench were charged desert prices, so they chose to thank Hashem instead and learned who He is. Then a boy named Chaim buys a cupcake and asks why he must make a brachah on something he paid for. His father takes him to the baker, who admits he paid only for work, not for the eggs and flour Hashem created. So we pay twice: money to the baker and a clear, careful brachah to Hashem. This leads to the second half of a story begun the week before. Rabbi Moshe Galante agrees to trade knowledge with an Arab sheikh who always knows whether a sick person will recover. After days of fasting and immersion, the sheikh shows him a splendid hidden shrine with the words 'I place Hashem before me always' set in jewels, and explains that the Name shines brightly when a sick person will live. Rabbi Moshe goes home ashamed that a gentile honored Hashem's Name more than he did, and from then on he thinks of Hashem every time he says a brachah.
display.lesson: Food belongs to Hashem, and a brachah is how we pay Him for it; say every brachah clearly and think about Whose Name you are saying.

advisories.note: The sheikh prays for sick people and can tell whether they will live or die; no particular case is described.

sources_cited.note: Avraham's 'eshel' in Be'er Sheva: eating, drinking and lodging or escorting; guests who would not bench were charged.
'The earth and all it contains belong to Hashem.'
Eating without a brachah is like stealing from Hashem (as cited).

segments.title: Avraham Avinu's tent in the desert
segments.summary: Avraham's guests could pay desert prices or thank Hashem, and so they learned about Him.

segments.title: Chaim's cupcake: paying twice
segments.summary: A visit to the baker shows that we pay people for their work, and pay Hashem with a brachah.

segments.title: Rabbi Moshe Galante and the sheikh's secret, second half
segments.summary: The sheikh reveals the jeweled Name of Hashem he prays before, and Rabbi Moshe resolves to honor Hashem's Name in every brachah.
